When she opened her eyes, Julian was standing at the courtyard entrance.
He wore black, as usual, the gold embroidery along his coat catching faint light from the windows.
"Are you planning to stand there until you freeze?"
When he reached her, he brushed snow gently from her hair and shoulders.
For a second, everything became impossibly quiet.
Julian seemed to realize what he was doing.
Julian seemed to realize what he'd admitted.
"The Crown Prince was expected to succeed him."
"His brother has marched troops into the capital."
She asked the question she knew Julian was waiting for.
Julian looked almost reluctant to answer.
"For the Crown Prince and his brother to weaken each other."
"The moment he agreed to trade me for soldiers, I let him go."
"I'll send you home when this is over."
He seemed almost angry with himself.
"I promise your reputation will remain untouched. No one will be able to accuse you of anything."
"Whatever happens between Adrian and his brothers, I'll end our arrangement afterward."
Snow continued falling long after he disappeared.
Escaping from home on the day of the festival.
But in the dream she did not go directly toward the crowded market.
She stopped beside an unfamiliar house.
Someone was crying behind a locked garden door.
A child's voice came cautiously from the other side.
Claire pressed her hand against the wooden door.
"Normal people don't have eyes like that."
Claire spoke with the absolute confidence of a child who had never considered that she might be wrong.
"So I think your eyes must be beautiful."
The other side of the door remained quiet.
"Next time I'll bring you a painting."
"My teacher says I paint horses well."
That was the memory she had carried for years.
The boy behind the door disappeared beneath it.
When Claire woke, tears covered her face.
For several seconds, she simply stared into the darkness.
She had met him before Adrian.
She had helped him before Adrian had ever saved her.
Something Claire had forgotten completely had become, for another person, a memory important enough to shape an entire life.
By morning, she knew one thing.

sections.title: Chapter Seventeen
paragraphs: She did not see him for seven days.
His Highness had matters of state.
Claire received the news with less emotion than she expected.
What she wanted to know was where Julian was.
Claire was sitting in the courtyard when a man walked through the snow.
The Crown Prince and the second prince had exhausted each other.
Adrian had struck afterward with overwhelming speed.
Arden's covert support and the political weight of House Ashford helped secure his victory.
Adrian looked at Claire and felt something surge inside him.
He mistook all of it for love.
During Claire's absence, he had begun to understand how much of his life she had quietly held together.
Westbridge House continued to function because of systems Claire had built.
His popularity survived because of work Claire had done.
People praised him for kindness that had often originated with her.
And during the fighting, Nathaniel Brooks had been killed after aligning himself with the losing faction.
Adrian had thought about that too.
He had loved Evelyn for ten years.
But now he believed he loved Claire as well.
Evelyn could remain near him as his royal companion.
Everyone he loved would have a place beside him.
Why shouldn't he have everything else too?
For the first time, he noticed her expression.
Adrian told himself she was merely hurt.
"I told you I'd make everything right."
"When you gave me away, Westbridge House stopped being my home."
"Before I left, I placed separation papers among my personal belongings."
"You're angry. Fine. You've made your point."
The contrast between them was almost theatrical.
Julian's pale eyes were colder than Claire had ever seen them.
"This has nothing to do with you."
"You've been here enjoying his attention, and now suddenly you're defending him?"
Blood appeared at the corner of his mouth.
For several seconds, no one moved.
"And you haven't even been crowned yet."
And somehow that enraged Adrian even more.
His next words came out almost desperate.
For the first time, Adrian looked genuinely afraid.
Because he had finally asked the one question he had always believed he knew the answer to.
And Claire no longer looked like a woman in love.

sections.title: Chapter Eighteen
paragraphs: Slowly, she turned back toward Adrian.
"You don't love me anymore?" Adrian asked.
His voice had lost all the anger from moments before.
For the first time, it sounded uncertain.
She said it with such calm finality that Adrian seemed unable to understand it.
And that frightened him more than hatred ever could.
Hatred still meant someone mattered enough to wound you.
But Claire looked at him as though he belonged to a life that had already ended.
He found no trace of the girl who had once watched him across crowded rooms.
This time, she entered the house.
And for the first time, he understood that a door could close long before someone physically walked away.
A newly victorious king could not remain abroad chasing a woman who had refused to return with him. Valeria was unstable, the court divided, and entire ministries awaited his decisions.
Once he was gone, the estate became peaceful again.
Julian did not visit Claire immediately.
For an entire morning, he stood outside the courtyard wondering whether he should go in.
Instead, when Claire noticed him, she looked almost... lighter.
"Unless Arden's princes have suddenly decided tea is beneath them."
For several minutes he said nothing.
"I have people watching over them discreetly. If anything happens, you'll know immediately."
"Do you really intend never to return to him?"
The answer came much too quickly.
"I mean... I want you to be happy."
Julian realized what he had said and the tips of his ears reddened.
"Not necessarily in the way that sounded."
Claire rested her chin lightly against her hand.
"If someone overheard you," she continued, "they might think Prince Julian Arden had fallen hopelessly in love with me."
His silence made her smile fade.
Julian looked at her for a long time.
"And I won't ask for anything now."
"If one day you decide you want to return to Valeria, I'll let you go."
A trace of pain entered his expression, but he did not hide from it.
"But if leaving is what makes you happy, I won't stop you."
Claire turned toward the bare tree in the courtyard.
The flowering tree Julian had planted because he'd remembered she once liked them.
"I'm tired of waiting for it to bloom."
By evening, the tree was gone.
Back in Valeria, Adrian's life had become everything he once wanted.
Ministers waiting outside his office for hours just to speak with him.
The royal residence was in chaos.
Evelyn stood in one of the private apartments surrounded by broken porcelain and torn books.
"How can you treat me like this?"
"I told you. The timing is wrong."
"I cannot appoint a royal consort before I appoint a queen."
"She was already part of my household."
Evelyn had imagined the future very differently.
She had expected Adrian to finally bring her beside him openly.
Perhaps she would not become queen.
Evelyn had never wanted the exhausting duties of a queen anyway.
The certainty that she remained the woman he loved most.
Courtiers looked at her with thinly disguised contempt.
Once, that question would have broken him.
He would have crossed the room immediately.
Now, he found himself remembering another woman.
Claire would never have thrown porcelain.
Claire would have understood the political situation before he'd finished explaining it.
Claire would already have organized the household, anticipated rumors, and solved half the problems creating his headache.
The comparison rose before he could stop it.
And suddenly Evelyn's tears seemed less romantic than they once had.
Evelyn had been the great love of his life.
So why, now that she was finally within reach—
was the woman he could not stop thinking about Claire?
When Claire had belonged to him, he'd wanted Evelyn.
and Claire had become the one thing he could no longer have.

sections.title: Chapter Nineteen
paragraphs: Winter slowly loosened its grip on Arden.
The old flowering tree was replaced with a young winter-plum tree.
One afternoon, she was tending to it when Julian approached from behind and placed a hand warmer into her hands.
She held the warmer against her palms.
"No one has done it very often."
Something in his expression tightened painfully.
Claire reached into her coat and produced an envelope.
Julian tucked it safely inside his coat.
He turned so quickly that Claire caught the edge of his cloak.
Claire still held the fabric between her fingers.
Her cheeks were pink from the cold.
He pulled her into his arms.
Julian immediately regretted moving so suddenly.
But he could not make himself let go.
He had spent ten years imagining this woman.
Ten years building a future around a girl who had once spoken to him through a closed door and forgotten him afterward.
Give her everything she had never received.
If he confessed, she might reject him.
If he stayed silent, he would slowly lose his mind.
Claire looked directly into his eyes.
"You should marry someone who can stand beside you without scandal."
His voice trembled despite his effort to control it.
He caught her wrist when she reached to straighten his collar.
But not in the way Claire expected.
"Does it hurt me to think another man touched you?"
"It makes me jealous enough to feel sick."
"But not because you are somehow less worthy."
"I'm jealous because you loved someone before me."
"Because someone else got years of your heart while I stood far away knowing almost nothing about your life."
His forehead lowered against her shoulder.
"I had no power when I was younger."
"So I told myself it was enough just knowing you existed somewhere."
"I used politics to bring you here."
"I told myself I'd give you a few peaceful months and then let you go."
"I don't want to let you go anymore."
"But if you ask me to, I will."
"Don't speak about yourself as though you're damaged."
"I spent ten years trying to become someone worthy of the girl behind that door."
A tear slid down Claire's cheek.
He tried to turn away, embarrassed by the tears in his own eyes.
Instead, she leaned forward and pressed a soft kiss near the corner of his eye.
"You're the first man who ever cried because he was afraid of losing me."
He pulled her into his arms so quickly she almost laughed.
He kissed the top of her head.
Claire closed her eyes and wrapped her arms around him.
It had been a very long time since happiness had felt this uncomplicated.

sections.title: Chapter Twenty
paragraphs: Now Queen Mother rather than Queen, she received him in her private apartments.
Adrian stood outside the door far longer than necessary.
He already knew why she'd called.
And Adrian had no way to explain the truth without admitting something monstrous.
I exchanged the woman who should have been queen for military support.
"Whatever your personal feelings were, that girl gave you everything."
"It's not that I refuse to make her queen."
Adrian took too long to answer.
Understanding slowly appeared in her face.
"Do you remember when I once summoned Claire to speak with me?"
"I told her not to repeat my mistake."
His mother looked toward the window.
"When I was young, I loved your father."
"There was another man who treated me far better."
She gestured around the luxurious room.
"Everything people told me should make a woman fortunate."
"I spent my life inside a palace sharing my husband's affection with other women."
"I won everything except the life I might actually have wanted."
"So I told Claire not to bury herself on the same road."
His mother's eyes said she understood.
His mother rarely used cruel language.
She did not need to raise her voice.
"You sent your lawful wife to another kingdom because you wanted a crown."
"And now that she has made her choice, you suddenly remember that you love her?"
"If you possess any affection for her at all, stop demanding that she spend the rest of her life paying for the fact that she once loved you."
Back in his office, Adrian destroyed everything within reach.
Adrian struck the desk hard enough to split the skin across his knuckles.
Why was everyone saying Claire had made a mistake?
She had been the one who insisted on marrying him.
How could she decide it was over?
No one else could be queen.
No one else could support him the way she had.
Claire's parents already knew the truth.
They knew she had chosen not to return.
They also knew exactly what Adrian had done.
General Ashford had still supported Adrian during the succession crisis because civil war was larger than one family's grief.
But that did not mean he had forgiven him.
"She went to enormous lengths to marry me. Now she thinks she can simply leave?"
Fear battled anger on her face.
"She heard that the former Crown Prince intended to destroy you."
"She begged her father for that marriage because she believed marrying you would force your enemies to hesitate."
"She knelt in our courtyard for hours."
"She never asked House Ashford to fight your political battles."
"She used our name as a shield."
"Because she was afraid you would be killed."
"You saved her when she was a child."
Something so insignificant in his own memory that he had barely thought of it afterward.
The accusation that she had forced him into marriage for ambition.
Because there was no version of the story left in which he was the wronged man.
And he had answered devotion with humiliation until nothing remained.
Cold spread through Adrian's entire body.
And for the first time, he understood the most terrifying part.
Claire wasn't waiting for him to become better.

sections.title: Chapter Twenty-One
paragraphs: When Claire asked Julian what he intended to do now, his answer came far too easily.
"You say that as though we're deciding what to have for dinner."
"I've thought about it for ten years. I don't require additional deliberation."
Soon afterward, she moved from the secluded estate into Julian's own residence.
Only then did she begin to understand how much his position in Arden had changed.
The unwanted foreign-looking prince of his childhood was gone.
The Crown Prince was weak, indecisive, and deeply unpopular.
Arden's king had increasingly transferred responsibilities to Julian.
Among ministers, the assumption was already clear.
Claire sometimes wondered what the past ten years had cost him.
How much effort had been required to transform himself from an expendable child into the kingdom's most capable heir.
She was thinking about it one evening while brushing her hair.
A hand gently took the brush from hers.
"Why don't you let a maid do this?"
He began slowly drawing the brush through her hair.
"Are all men in Arden this shamelessly direct?"
Claire watched him through the mirror.
Once, she would have considered this kind of quiet intimacy impossible.
Simply someone brushing her hair because he wanted to.
Someone looking at her as though caring for her was not a burden to be repaid—
And strangely, that frightened her far less than love ever had before.

sections.title: Chapter Twenty-One — Continued
paragraphs: Julian finished brushing Claire's hair and set the brush down on the dressing table.
Then, almost as though he'd only just remembered it, he reached inside his coat.
The handwriting on the front made her sit straighter immediately.
"You wrote to your family. This is their reply."
Claire broke the seal at once.

Her mother assured her that both she and General Ashford were well. The capital had finally begun to settle after the succession crisis, though Adrian's government remained overwhelmed with the work of rebuilding order.
There were other pieces of news too.
Adrian still had not chosen a queen.
The ministers were beginning to complain openly about the delay.

Rumors had also spread concerning Evelyn Brooks, the young widow whom Adrian had quietly brought into the royal residence without publicly establishing her position. His reputation had suffered for it.
And then there was one final paragraph.
Claire's mother explained what had happened—how she had finally told him the truth about the marriage, and how Adrian had stood there in shock before leaving without anger or threat.
Don't worry about us,* her mother wrote. *Everything here is fine.
Your father and I ask for nothing except that you remain healthy, safe, and happy.
Then she folded the letter carefully and placed it inside a small wooden box.
"The one that says you're offended simply because I said his name."
Julian made no effort to deny it.
"Why hasn't he made Evelyn queen?" she wondered aloud. "It's what he always wanted."
"Perhaps he didn't want her as much as everyone—including himself—believed."
"Or perhaps he's incapable of wanting one thing at a time."
There was enough irritation in his voice to make Claire laugh again.
He leaned closer with shameless seriousness.
"If jealousy doesn't trouble you, then I intend to be jealous openly."
"I don't like him. And I don't like seeing you sit here thinking about him."
"Then what would you prefer I think about?"
Claire reached up and brushed a loose strand of hair away from his forehead.
"About what the last ten years must have been like for you."
Her hand remained near his temple.
This time, Julian did not tease her.
Claire wondered if she'd gone too far.
"There were years when I honestly thought I wouldn't survive long enough for any of it to matter."
"I believed that if I endured long enough, eventually it would be worth something."
His pale eyes settled on her.
And Claire found herself smiling too.
In Valeria, Evelyn was becoming frightened.
After Adrian's visit to Ashford Hall, he had changed.
He spent nearly all his time inside his office.
Outside official appearances, he rarely visited any of the private royal apartments.
Adrian had summoned Lily to his study and kept her there for a long conversation.
No one knew what they discussed.
Servants claimed that at some point Adrian became angry enough to smash something.
That made Evelyn even more uneasy.
She hated the sensation of losing something she had once considered unquestionably hers.
Evelyn remained outside his office in the winter cold and made it clear she would stand there all day if necessary.
The moment she entered, she dismissed the servants.
She placed a small box of pastries on the desk.
"You've been working constantly. You need to take better care of yourself."
"Do you remember the first time we met?"
"That was the first moment I fell for you."
"Afterward, I told Claire that one day I would marry you."
"For ten years, I convinced myself you loved me too."
"You never once clearly told me that you loved me."
"You kept me close enough to hope."
"But never close enough to be certain."
"A little jealousy at exactly the right moment."
Evelyn's face began to lose color.
"And I find that I hate the idea that you knew how much I loved you and used it because you enjoyed being loved."
she knew he was not entirely wrong.
Perhaps even loved him in her own way.
But she had also loved the attention.
There had always been men around Evelyn.
She had perfected the ability to give someone just enough hope to keep them interested.
Never anything she could be blamed for.
At her wedding to Nathaniel, she'd secretly wondered whether Adrian would appear and stop the ceremony.
That had disappointed her more than she liked to admit.
Then at the Spring Assembly, she had deliberately allowed him to follow her into the corridor.
She had known exactly what she was doing.
She had known Claire would hate seeing it.
A small part of her had wanted Claire to see.
Because Claire's perfect composure irritated her.
Because even after Evelyn married another man, some selfish part of her still wanted proof that Adrian belonged emotionally to her.
When Claire found them, Evelyn needed only to look wounded and walk away.
Adrian would become the guilty one.
That was how it had always worked.
Now Adrian was looking directly at something Evelyn herself preferred not to examine.
"Then why did you never choose me?"
A moment later, Adrian summoned his chief aide.
"In seven days, I'm going to Arden."
Adrian stared down at his desk.

sections.title: Chapter Twenty-Two
paragraphs: News that the newly crowned King Adrian of Valeria intended to make a personal diplomatic visit to Arden caused a sensation.
Julian's first thought was not diplomacy.
He spent nearly an entire evening deciding how to tell her.
When he finally did, Claire barely reacted.
She looked up from her book.
A smile slowly spread across his face.
"Already acting like the mistress of the house."
"Try not to miss me too badly."
Arden's Crown Prince and Julian formally received him before escorting the Valerian delegation to the royal palace.
"You think she stays because she loves you?"
"You found her at the moment she was hurt and confused."
"And now you've convinced yourself she chose you."
"You don't get to decide for her anymore."
"If you don't want her to spend the rest of her life hating you, I suggest you accept that."
"You're speaking boldly for a man who abducted the Queen of Valeria."
"Would you like me to remind you who offered her to me?"
The two men stared at each other.
A servant announced the arrival of Arden's king before either could say more.
The formal meeting that followed was cordial.
By the end, Adrian appeared perfectly composed.
Yet as he left, he gave Julian one final look.
Something in it made Julian's stomach tighten.
He left the palace almost immediately.
He rode home faster than protocol allowed.
When he reached Claire's courtyard, the gate stood open.
One of the servants lay unconscious near the entrance.
Claire woke inside a moving carriage.
The scent still clung faintly to her clothes.
They had pressed a treated cloth over her mouth before she could call for help.
Instead, her hand moved to her hair.
Claire pulled out a metal hairpin and lunged.
He caught her wrist inches from his face.
The pin fell and snapped beneath their feet.
"I told you not to come for me."
The anger vanished from his face.
He released some pressure on her wrist.
"And yet I convinced myself that if I gave you enough..."
"I thought if I tried hard enough, we could still have a good ending."
"But not everything returns what you give it."
She had spent years believing perseverance must eventually be rewarded.
Sometimes persistence was only another name for refusing to accept the answer.
"I did everything I knew how to do."
"And I have nothing left to prove."
That sentence broke something in him.
His grip tightened around her hand again.
"I was the one who made you fall in love with me."
"You were supposed to stay beside me for the rest of your life."
The words that had once seemed impossible for him to say.
And now they came only when they no longer mattered.
For a long time, she said nothing.
"You were right about one thing on our wedding night."
"We could each have married someone else and lived perfectly good lives."
Claire returned them to him now.
Adrian looked as though she had struck him.
"So the rest of my life cannot keep being about you."
Adrian stared at her as though he could no longer breathe.
how exactly was he supposed to carry all those memories and still live well?
Then the door was torn open.
One hand gripped the carriage frame.
Claire stumbled directly into his arms.
The faint smell of horse and cold air and sweat.
She wrapped her arms around him.
Claire closed her eyes against his chest.
"If it's you, I can forgive being a little late."
Inside the carriage, Adrian remained in shadow.
Adrian looked broken now rather than angry.
"But don't I deserve one chance to do better?"
At the man beside her who was trying very hard not to beg her with his eyes.
Then Claire looked back into the carriage.
"There is one person I refuse to betray for the rest of my life."
For perhaps the first time in his life, Prince Julian Arden visibly blushed.
From his ears all the way down his neck.
This time, when Claire walked away—
he finally understood that chasing her would not bring her back.

sections.title: Chapter Twenty-Three
paragraphs: Two years later, Julian Arden became king.
By then, he and Claire had been married for a year.
Their wedding had been impossible to ignore.
Claire had once left one marriage hidden in darkness, treated almost like something to be traded away.
The cathedral bells rang across the capital.
Every major noble house in Arden was present.
Claire walked through the cathedral doors in white and gold, not as a secret, not as a political deposit, not as a woman someone had reluctantly accepted—
but as the future queen Julian had chosen openly.
Julian had somehow managed to bring her from Valeria.
The moment Anna saw Claire again, she burst into tears.
Julian handled everything else with the same maddening efficiency.
Her previous marriage was legally recognized as dissolved.
No stain was permitted to attach itself to her name.
By the time Julian inherited the throne, the public story was simple enough:
The king had fallen in love with a foreign noblewoman.
That last part required no political explanation.
There were no royal favorites hidden in distant wings of the palace.
No women waiting for his affection.
One evening, Claire sat before her mirror brushing her hair.
As always, another hand eventually stole the brush.
"You truly are obsessed with my hair."
He bent and kissed lightly near her ear.
They had been married for a year.
And still, there was one boundary neither had crossed.
Their wedding night had passed quietly.
He never asked when she would be ready.
So they slept beside each other.
Sometimes Claire fell asleep against his shoulder.
Her body still remembered another night.
Fear had a remarkable way of surviving after the person who created it was gone.
But because she wanted something different now.
She wanted the memory to stop deciding things for her.
That night, Julian joined her as usual.
Then, with carefully manufactured casualness, she said:
"You could at least let me finish."
"It might save you from having to spend every night here."
"You're aware I enjoy spending every night here."
"I have never said anything of the sort."
Claire put down the teapot with exaggerated annoyance.
"What else would you like your wife to do?"
"I don't want you to do anything because you think you owe me."
Julian seemed almost afraid to believe her.
Only when she reached for his hand did he move.
And that night, for the first time, Claire discovered that intimacy did not have to feel like fear.
Only tenderness so intense that at first Claire almost didn't know what to do with it.
At one point, Julian whispered against her skin:
"Have I told you how beautiful you are?"
His voice was warm with happiness.
Later, when sleep finally began pulling her under, one unexpected thought passed through her mind.
So this was what it could have been.
And for once, the realization did not make her mourn the past.
It only made her grateful for the present.
Adrian eventually appointed another woman as queen—the daughter of a respected general.
The decision did little to repair his reputation.
They remembered the wife who had stood beside him before he became king.
No official explanation for her disappearance was ever entirely convincing, and rumors spread that Adrian had abandoned his first wife after taking the throne.
Evelyn and Lily both received formal positions within the royal household.
Yet Adrian visited Lily more often.
Perhaps because she contained pieces of two women he had lost in different ways.
But her quiet temperament reminded him of Claire.
Adrian sometimes found himself sitting across from Lily in silence, searching for expressions that did not belong to her.
"What did Claire say about me when I wasn't there?"
"She simply did what needed to be done."
He still woke sometimes in the middle of the night.
Memories came more clearly now than they had when Claire was beside him.
The look on her face after he struck her.
The moment she refused to follow him home.
So he did the only thing he could still do.
He promoted Claire's brothers according to merit.
He made certain her parents were respected.
He protected the charities Claire had established.
Perhaps some pathetic part of him believed kindness offered to the people she loved might eventually travel far enough to reach her.
One day Adrian returned to St. Aurelia's Abbey.
Father Benedict was preparing to leave on a long pilgrimage.
The old priest looked even older now.
His gaze wandered across the familiar stone courtyard.
He had been here with Claire.
When nothing had yet gone wrong.
Father Benedict considered how best to explain it.
"Her family was told when she was born that her life would be difficult."
Adrian remembered Claire's strange childhood superstition.
"She came to me many times because she believed certain relationships might change the course of that life."
"After she married you, she repeatedly asked whether the path before her had changed."
Father Benedict did not answer immediately.
"I told her more than once that it had not."
Adrian felt something cold move down his spine.
"That the person beside her was not the person who would lead her toward peace."
"Recently, however, I considered her situation again."
The old priest gathered his things.
"It appears she finally found the right companion."
The words repeated inside his head.
Wanted to insist that Claire had belonged beside him.
That Julian had stolen something that should have been his.
But reality had become impossible to argue with.
And Adrian had never given her that.
He walked through the abbey until he reached a quiet corner of the grounds.
Years ago, he'd built a ridiculous trap there.
Adrian had turned toward someone else.
And, in a way, he had never truly turned back until there was nobody behind him anymore.
No little girl watching him as though he were the entire world.
Adrian stood there for a long time.
The day was clear and windless.
Somewhere, two people had found one another.
Somewhere else, someone had discovered love only after losing it.
Another learned to live with regret.
The world did not wait for anyone to understand their mistakes.

sections.title: Epilogue One — Julian
paragraphs: For most of his childhood, Julian believed there was something shameful about his existence.

He had watched his mother endure the quiet cruelty of women with higher rank and stronger families. He had heard servants whisper about her foreign accent, her background, the fact that she had once been a dancer rather than a noblewoman.
Sometimes, late at night, he heard her crying.
Once, when Julian was very young, she gripped his arm so tightly that her nails nearly broke the skin.
"If only you didn't have my eyes," she whispered through tears. "If only you looked more like your father."
He only tried to reach for her.
That was when he first understood something no child should understand so young.
He was a prince in name, nothing more.
When Julian was eleven, he was sent to Valeria as a political hostage.
He remembered the carriage pulling away from the palace.
His mother's voice came from somewhere outside.
"Did His Majesty truly say that if I agreed to this, he might visit me again?"
That was the last time Julian ever saw her alive.
Everyone knew he was an unwanted prince from a foreign kingdom.
Other royal children mocked his eyes.
The fact that Arden had apparently considered him expendable enough to send away.
A hostage did not have that luxury.
One afternoon, several boys from the royal family decided it would be amusing to lock him inside an abandoned building at the edge of an old estate.
They pushed him through the door.
Julian pounded against the wood until his hands hurt.
The room smelled of mold and wet stone.
He sank against the door, hugged his knees to his chest, and cried.
His mother had always told him not to cry.
Tears made people think you were weak.
Worse, she had once told him that his strange pale eyes looked especially ugly when filled with tears.
But that day Julian no longer cared.
A thought appeared in his mind.
Perhaps it would be easier if I simply disappeared.
Then someone knocked from the other side of the door.
A child hearing someone cry behind a door and deciding to ask whether they were all right.
Julian remembered it for the next ten years.
She had never even seen his face.
She did not ask why he was hiding.
She did not demand to know who he was.
Then, when he reluctantly confessed that people hated the unusual color of his eyes, she told him something absurdly simple.
Therefore, his eyes must be beautiful.
Julian had been mocked, dismissed, and treated like an inconvenience for as long as he could remember.
One little girl told him he was beautiful without even seeing him.
A year later, Julian returned to Arden.
No one would even tell him where she had been buried.
Julian knew very little about royal intrigue then.
Powerlessness had taken everything from him.
So when ambitious officials approached the unwanted young prince and offered to support him for their own purposes, Julian accepted immediately.
Perhaps they intended to use him.
If there was a rope leading upward, he would climb it even if every strand cut his hands open.
His father still disliked looking at him.
The pale eyes reminded the king too much of Julian's mother.
But disdain no longer frightened him.
He learned exactly when to appear harmless.
The men who first supported him believed they were creating something they could control.
Years later, they discovered they were wrong.
By then, Julian had dismantled their faction completely.
The last of those men looked up at him bitterly and said:
"We chose you precisely because no one wanted you."
"You had no mother's family behind you. No one loved you. You were perfect."
"You think you've escaped that? You're still the same abandoned piece on the board."
Then he ended the man's life.
Several days later, Julian learned that his father intended to send him to Valeria as part of a diplomatic delegation.
For the first time in years, the thought made him nervous.
Then his agents brought him news.
Lady Claire Ashford had married Prince Adrian Vale.
Julian locked himself inside his study.
He spent an embarrassing amount of time staring at nothing.
He had carried one girl's voice in his memory for ten years.
How could someone else simply arrive first?
For several furious hours, Julian imagined every reckless way he could take her away.
Because all of those plans had the same ending.
That mattered more than anything else.
So he made himself a promise.
If she was happy, he would leave her alone.
At the Spring Assembly, Julian finally saw her face for the first time.
But that was not what struck him most.
A dress elegant without demanding attention.
He used the formal toasts as an excuse to approach her table.
When he stood before her, close enough to see her eyes clearly, he forgot half of what he had intended to say.
So instead he warned her that the Arden wine was too strong.
He walked away absurdly pleased with himself.
Then one of his men came quietly to report that Adrian had followed another woman into a corridor while Claire was alone in the palace garden.
Julian went to the garden immediately.
He pretended the meeting was accidental.
All while looking at Claire far more than was appropriate.
Then, subtly, he guided the conversation and their position so that when Claire returned toward the ballroom, she would pass the corridor where Adrian stood with Evelyn.
Julian knew exactly what he was doing.
He hated Adrian for betraying Claire.
And some selfish part of him was glad.
perhaps there was still a place for him in her life.
The request for a painting of horses.
Every one of those things was an attempt to make her remember.
For a while, Julian almost accepted defeat.
And Julian saw one final opening.
He allowed information to reach Adrian's advisers.
Arden might be willing to support Adrian's claim to the throne.
Julian sat across from Claire's husband and forced himself to smile.
"Naturally, support like that has a price."
Adrian told him to name it.
Julian nearly crushed the cup in his hand.
And in that moment, he knew.
A guarantee that Adrian would uphold his side of the political arrangement.
When Claire was brought to Julian's carriage, still asleep, he sat across from her for a very long time.
He touched a loose strand of hair near her face.
He had imagined meeting her again for a decade.
He had never imagined it would happen like this.
Nor did he dare tell Claire how much she meant to him.
So when Claire woke, Julian hid everything behind humor.
Those months in Arden became the happiest Julian had ever known.
No matter how exhausting the day had been, there was always one place he wanted to return to.
Before visiting her, he always washed carefully.
If there had been blood on him from political violence or military matters, he made certain not even the smell remained.
Walked into her house pretending he had not spent the entire day waiting for that moment.
Like a ridiculous bird displaying its finest feathers.
And every time Claire smiled at him, he went home believing the entire struggle of his life might have been worth it.
When he told Claire about Adrian's eventual victory, his nails dug into his own palms.
He expected her to ask to return immediately.
When Adrian came to take her home, Julian feared she would go.
Each time, a little of the terror eased.
Perhaps she even cared for him.
Then came the afternoon when Claire tried to push him away.
She told him he deserved someone better.
Everything Julian had buried since childhood came rushing back.
For the first time since childhood, his eyes filled with tears.
Never let anyone see weakness in those eyes.
But Claire kissed the corner of one.
She told him not to betray her.
Years later, after they were married, Claire once asked:
Julian thought about telling her the truth.
That he'd been terrified she would abandon him.
That he'd been afraid she would look at his desperation and see something pathetic.
Instead, he kissed the tip of her nose.
And somehow, that sound seemed to fill every empty year between the frightened boy behind the locked door—
and the man holding her now.
For Julian, it had all been worth it.

sections.title: Epilogue Two — Adrian
paragraphs: Adrian learned something important when he was very young.
His mother did not love his father.
Unlike the other women at court, she never fought desperately for the king's affection.
She watched those rivalries with detached amusement.
"What you can actually hold in your hands matters most."
"Don't spend your life chasing things that exist only in imagination."
"Learn to keep what is already yours."
And Adrian had fallen in love.
Evelyn Hart was unlike every other girl he knew.
She did not care about perfect posture or quiet voices.
How could anyone not love someone like her?
One of his clearest memories came from a lantern festival in their youth.
But only because going with Claire provided an excuse to secretly meet Evelyn.
Music and laughter came from every direction.
Adrian turned instinctively and caught her.
He positioned himself between Claire and the pushing crowd like an older brother protecting a younger sister.
His hands remained briefly on her shoulders.
But his eyes were already searching for Evelyn again.
Then she tugged gently at his sleeve.
"Maybe we could look at the festival while we wait."
She pointed toward a booth with puzzles and lanterns.
"What if Evelyn comes and can't find us?"
Colored paper drifted through the air around her as performers passed in procession.
Adrian's young heart seemed to stop.
Then felt someone holding his sleeve.
She was standing perfectly straight, fingers still curled around the fabric.
For one brief moment, Adrian noticed how lovely she was becoming.
Then he leaned toward her and whispered:
"One day, I'm going to marry Evelyn."
The light in Claire's expression changed.
"You'll be happy for me, won't you?"
He simply removed her fingers from his sleeve and walked toward Evelyn.
As Adrian grew older, politics complicated everything.
His father taught him that every friendship could look like an alliance.
Every visit could be interpreted as a political statement.
Being close to the Ashfords might make the Crown Prince suspicious.
Visiting the wrong minister might create rumors.
Doing nothing, however, meant allowing other princes to gather power while he remained vulnerable.
Yet sometimes, he imagined abandoning all of it.
Then the king announced Adrian's marriage.
He had deliberately reduced contact with the Ashfords to avoid political suspicion.
She knew he intended to marry Evelyn.
Hadn't she once stood beside him while he said so?
The anger grew until, on their wedding night, Adrian left Claire alone and went secretly to Evelyn.
Evelyn looked surprised to see him.
But Adrian thought he saw something else in her eyes.
He held Evelyn in the darkness.
Surely no woman could reject that.
He had been prepared to surrender a crown.
And she told him to be reasonable.
"If you love me too, that's enough."
"You should go back to your wife."
That was when Adrian's anger toward Claire became hatred.
If Claire had not married him, Evelyn would have chosen him.
That was what he told himself.
It was easier than considering any other explanation.
Later, Adrian watched Evelyn marry Nathaniel.
He heard servants praising how happy she looked.
How pleased she was with the marriage.
And because he failed, he hurt Claire again and again.
By that time, Adrian had won the throne.
Her eyes were swollen from crying.
"What am I supposed to do now?"
Adrian looked at the woman he had loved—
He promised her a place beside him.
But the fantasy did not survive reality.
The more time they spent together, the more Adrian began noticing things he'd once refused to see.
Then one day, in the middle of another fight, Evelyn screamed:
"You loved me first! Why are you suddenly acting as though Claire was the great love of your life?"
"Even if I had become queen, it would only have been fair. She wanted your position too. She stole my place."
He left before she could explain.
She was making tea when Adrian entered without warning.
Then, to her shock, the king dropped to his knees.
Pressed his forehead against her lap.
Adrian didn't even realize what name he'd spoken.
Then rested her fingers against the side of his head.
It reminded Adrian painfully of someone else.
But Lily's words destroyed the illusion.
"She's been gone for a very long time."
Lily understood more than Adrian realized.
And perhaps that was precisely why Claire had selected her in the first place.
Lily had no intention of falling in love with him.
And out of respect for Claire, she would not pretend to be what Adrian wanted.
Still, she stroked his hair gently.
Adrian clutched the fabric of her gown.
He barely seemed to hear her.
would she touch him this gently?
Would she hold him while he admitted how badly he'd failed?
"Will anyone ever love me the way she did?"
"And I suspect the only person still grieving over what happened is you."
The truth was merciless precisely because she did not say it cruelly.
He finally understood his mother's lesson.
He had spent his life chasing what he could not possess.
And while chasing them, he had destroyed the one thing that had once been entirely real.
Now he possessed almost everything he'd wanted.
And none of it could buy back what he'd thrown away.
"If I could suffer enough to make her forgive me..."
She did not want anything from him.
A tear fell onto Lily's gown.
He did not know exactly what he was asking.
Why had he been so blind?
Why had he become so cruel?
Why had he won a kingdom only to feel as though he had lost everything worth having?
And somewhere far beyond Valeria, Claire was living a life that no longer contained him.
That, more than anything, was the punishment.
But that she was happy enough to stop looking back.
